S62.09.needs: two or more Work tasks running or queued at the same time
S62.09.note: The overview lists all of them, but the detail panel on the right follows only one selected task at a time. The sidebar has no Work history entry; the route is /tasks, reached here through the command palette or the "Active" section on the Chat home screen.
steps: Press Command+K to open the command palette, then type "Work history" in the "Search chats and actions" box and press Enter on the "Work history" result.
On the Work history page, keep the filter on "Active" and check that each running or queued Work task has its own row, with a small live dot on the running ones.
Click the "Board" button in the layout control at the top right of the list.
Compare the rows or cards: several running tasks should be visible together in one view, not one at a time.
S62.09.where: Command+K (Ctrl+K on Windows) > type "Work history" > Work history. Then look at the list (the default filter is "Active"); "Board" is the second layout button, next to the "List" one.

S62.10.needs: one Work task that is waiting for approval and one that is still running
S62.10.note: The code treats awaiting_input, awaiting_approval and paused as needing input and moves those rows to the top of the list. The top-of-list placement is set in code and is not a separate visible label.
steps: Start two Work tasks, one that will ask for approval and one that keeps running, then open Work history from Command+K > "Work history".
With the filter on "Active", look at the top of the list: a task waiting for approval or paused should appear above the running ones.
Click the "Needs you" button in the filter control at the top of the list.
Compare: only tasks that need your input should be shown, and they should be the first rows.
S62.10.where: Work history > filter "Needs you" (or the unfiltered list, where these tasks are placed first)

S62.11.needs: a Work task that is waiting for your approval
S62.11.note: The inline unblock is for approval requests only. The "Message the agent" box in the task details panel is a separate steering control for live tasks.
steps: Open Work history (Command+K > "Work history") and keep the list on the first page.
Find the task whose card says "Waiting for your approval". Optionally type a note in the box "Guidance for this work session".
Click "Approve" (or "Deny") on that card, without opening the task details.
Compare: the card should show a short busy spinner, then the task should move on, and you should still be on the Work history list.
S62.11.where: Work history > a task card showing "Waiting for your approval" > Approve or Deny buttons on that card

S62.12.needs: a Work task that has already run, ideally one with more than 4,000 events
S62.12.note: The panel shows a summary of the activity and stops at 4,000 events. The code says the full record is in the source chat, so the panel itself is not a complete transcript; the tester should check this against Expected.
steps: Open Work history and click the title of any task row (it has an "View details for" label for screen readers).
On the right, the "Task details" panel opens with the goal, the plan, the latest output or result, and the activity list.
Scroll the panel to the bottom and read the note about events; if it says "Showing the first 4,000 events", click "Open source chat".
Compare: the chat that ran the task should open and show the conversation the task came from.
S62.12.where: Work history > click a task row > "Task details" panel > "Open source chat"

S62.17.needs: a conversation with at least one reply
S62.17.note: The branch icon on assistant replies appears only on hover, and the "Duplicate as branch" item is shown only when the conversation has messages.
steps: Open a conversation that has at least two messages and one assistant reply.
Hover under the assistant reply and click the icon button labelled "Branch conversation from here" (or click "More message actions" on a user message and choose "Branch conversation from here").
Wait for the toast "Conversation branch created"; the app opens the new chat.
Type a new message in the new chat and send it, then go back to the original chat.
Compare: the new branch should continue on its own and the original chat should be unchanged. The arrows "Previous branch" and "Next branch" should move between versions.
S62.17.where: Chat > open a conversation with an answer > hover under an assistant reply and click the branch icon (tooltip "Branch conversation: this chat stays unchanged"); or the conversation's "Conversation options" menu > "Duplicate as branch"
